itineraries.title: Albania Road Trip: Sea, Mountains & Complete Itinerary
itineraries.subtitle: From Tirana to Koman's fjords, from the Accursed Mountains to the Ionian Riviera
itineraries.climate: Best time to visit: June and September, with temperatures of 20 to 28°C on the coast and 15 to 22°C in the mountains. Avoid July-August (excessive coastal heat reaching 35-40°C and crowded beaches) and October-May for the crossing of the Valbona-Theth pass on foot, as it may be snow-covered. Winters on the coast are mild but very rainy.
specialties: Byrek (savory pie with cheese or spinach)

visits.text: Skanderbeg Square sprawls across 40,000 m², the largest pedestrian plaza in the Balkans. The dome of the history museum dominates the northern side, adorned with the giant mosaic “The Albanians,” created in 1981.

Bunk'Art 1 hides inside Mount Dajti: 106 rooms across five underground levels, built in the 1970s as a nuclear bunker for dictator Enver Hoxha. The galleries chronicle life under communist dictatorship.
Descend into Bunk'Art 2, a 1,000 m² bunker beneath the Interior Ministry. The Sigurimi (secret police) cells bear witness to political terror. Historical photographs illustrate communist persecution.

Built between 1791 and 1821, Et'hem Bey Mosque stands out for its rare frescoes: trees, waterfalls and bridges adorn the portico. On January 18, 1991, 10,000 people prayed here despite the ban, marking the end of state-imposed atheism.
The Orthodox Resurrection Cathedral was inaugurated in 2012. Its dome rises 32 meters, the bell tower reaches 46 meters. The 586 m² mosaics depict Christ Pantocrator.

activities.text: Walk up the Boulevard of National Martyrs from Skanderbeg Square to the Grand Park. The colorful buildings and urban energy illustrate Tirana's rapid transformation.

visits.text: Krujë Castle withstood the Ottomans three times (1450, 1466, 1467) under Skanderbeg. Mehmed II the Conqueror did not take the fortress until 1478, ten years after the national hero's death.

The Skanderbeg Museum, inaugurated in 1982, occupies a monumental building inspired by Albanian stone towers. Architects Pranvera Hoxha and Pirro Vaso designed this tribute to the hero who defied the Ottoman Empire for 25 years.
The old Ottoman bazaar winds along cobbled lanes. Artisans sell traditional embroidery, kilim rugs and copper objects. The wooden shops date from the Ottoman era.

activities.text: Climb up to the castle ramparts for the panoramic view. In clear weather, the Tirana plain stretches as far as the Adriatic Sea.

visits.text: Head to the pedestrian street Rruga Kole Idromeno, the beating heart of Shkodër. Colorful facades house cafés and bistros. Street art brings the walls to life. In the evening, locals gather at outdoor tables.

Rozafa Castle stands on a hill at the confluence of the Buna and Drin rivers. Founded by the Illyrians, rebuilt by the Venetians then the Ottomans, it retains its 14th-century walls. Legend has it that Rozafa was walled up alive to ensure the foundations' strength.

The Marubi National Photography Museum preserves 150,000 historical photographs. The collection begins with the first photograph taken in Albania in 1858 by Pjetër Marubi. Three generations of Marubi photographers documented Albanian life.

Lake Shkodra, the largest in the Balkans, straddles the border with Montenegro. The wetlands shelter 270 bird species, including pelicans. The village of Shiroka offers the closest access from the city.

activities.text: Rent a bike to reach Shiroka (30 minutes). The wooden bridge crosses the Buna, and the bike path runs along the green peninsula to the lake. Swimming is possible in the clear waters in summer.

practical_info.tip: Bike rental available at downtown hotels

to_next_leg.road_type: Route de Shkoder a Koman, ferry du lac de Koman jusqu'a Fierze, puis piste de la vallee jusqu'a Valbone

visits.text: The Koman ferry travels up the lake-fjord carved into the Albanian Alps. Rock walls plunge vertically into emerald waters. Isolated villages cling to cliffs, accessible only by boat. One of the most spectacular river journeys in Europe.

The Valbona Valley stretches for 25 km between the peaks of the Prokletije (Accursed Mountains). The national park, created in 1966, protects beech forests and alpine meadows. Jezerca Peak rises to 2,694 meters.

The trails in the Valbona Valley follow the river through meadows and forests. Limestone peaks tower above the banks and clearings. A late-afternoon walk to observe the turquoise water and mountain scenery.

activities.text: Early morning boarding at Koman (departure around 9am). The cruise to Fierza lasts 2.5-3 hours. Minibus from Fierza to Valbona (30 minutes). Arrival in early afternoon to enjoy the valley.

practical_info.tip: Book the ferry in advance during high season. Car left in Shkodër or parked at Koman.

activities.text: Acclimatization hike in Valbona Valley in late afternoon. Marked trails follow the turquoise river through meadows and forests. Dinner at the guesthouse with local produce.

to_next_leg.road_type: Sentier du col de Valbona a 1 792 metres, entre les deux vallees

visits.text: Theth National Park, created in 1966, protects 2,630 hectares of karst mountains. Traditional stone houses are scattered across the steep-sided valley. Isolation has preserved the mountain way of life for centuries.

The Kulla Tower (Kulla e Ngujimit) served as a refuge during blood feuds. According to the Kanun, Albania's traditional code, men threatened by a blood feud could hide here until the families reconciled. The restored tower now functions as a museum.

Grunas Waterfall plunges 30 meters into a turquoise basin. The walk from the village center takes 45 minutes through meadows and beech forests. A rainbow forms in front of the falls on sunny afternoons.

The Church of Theth, built in 1892, stands out for its simplicity: local stone, wooden roof, modest bell tower. Surrounded by meadows with views of the peaks, it's one of northern Albania's most photographed monuments.

activities.text: The Valbona-Theth trek via Valbona Pass (1,792 m) is the iconic hike of the Albanian Alps. Departure at dawn, gradual ascent to the pass, descent to Theth. Panoramic views over both valleys. Arrival in Theth in early afternoon.

practical_info.tip: Very early departure mandatory (7am). Guide recommended. Bring water, food, warm clothes.

to_next_leg.road_type: Descente de Theth sur Shkoder puis route vers le sud par Elbasan

visits.text: Pogradec stretches along the Albanian shore of Lake Ohrid. The café-lined promenade follows the water for several kilometers. Communist-era buildings stand beside recent construction. A restful stop after the northern mountains.

The Albanian shore of Lake Ohrid alternates between pebble beaches and reed beds. The UNESCO-listed lake shelters endemic species including the koran trout. Mountains drop down to the water. The border with North Macedonia cuts the lake in two.

activities.text: Return by jeep from Theth to Shkodër (2 hours). Pick up the car. Long drive to Pogradec via Elbasan (approximately 4 hours). A transfer day, offering welcome rest after the previous day's trek.

practical_info.tip: Jeep organized by Theth guesthouse, early departure. Lunch in Shkodër or on the road.

visits.text: Lake Ohrid, one of Europe's oldest lakes, straddles the border with North Macedonia. The UNESCO-listed lake is 288 meters deep and shelters over 200 endemic species including the koran trout, Pogradec's emblem.

The Lin peninsula projects into the lake, approximately 20 km from Pogradec, a 25-minute drive: recent excavations have revealed Europe's oldest lakeside settlement, dating back 8,500 years. The early Christian basilica from the 4th century preserves mosaics. A bunker converted into a chapel marks the tip.
Drilon National Park protects an area of karst springs feeding the lake. Crystal-clear waters wind between century-old oaks and plane trees. Trails border the natural channels.
The village of Tushemisht preserves traditional houses with red tile roofs. Multiple springs create small channels and ponds. Restaurants specialize in the lake's freshwater fish.

activities.text: Walk along Pogradec's promenade in late afternoon for the xhiro, the Albanian tradition of taking an evening stroll. Families gather, cafés buzz, views stretch across the lake to the Macedonian mountains.
Swim in the clear waters of Lake Ohrid from the beaches of Pogradec or Tushemisht. Pleasant temperature from July to September. Paddleboat and kayak rental available in summer.

visits.text: The white Ottoman houses of the Mangalem Quarter rise in tiers up the slope. Numerous windows (hence the nickname “city of a thousand windows”) catch the light on wooden balconies. Cobbled alleys, 18th-century mosques, the Halveti order's tekke dating from 1782.
The Gorica Bridge crosses the Osum in seven stone arches. Built in wood in 1780, rebuilt in stone in the 1920s, it links Mangalem to the Orthodox Christian quarter of Gorica.

The Gorica Quarter, traditionally Orthodox Christian, offers a calmer atmosphere. The 19th-century Saint Spyridon Church, Saint Thomas Church higher up the hillside. Stone houses, narrow alleys, views over Mangalem from the hill.

Berat Castle (Kalaja) has dominated the city since the 4th century BC. Rebuilt in the 13th century, it remains inhabited: families still live within the walls. Byzantine churches, Ottoman mosque, ramparts spanning 2,400 years of continuous occupation.

The Onufri Museum occupies the Dormition Cathedral inside the castle. Collection of Byzantine and post-Byzantine icons, works by painter Onufri (16th century) famous for his unique vermillion red. Carved woodwork, gilded iconostasis.

activities.text: Climb to the Gorica ruins on the hill opposite the castle. Panoramic view over both quarters, the bridge, the Osum and the mountains. Forest trail, 45 minutes round trip.

visits.text: Gjirokastër Castle, one of the largest in the Balkans, was built in the 12th century then rebuilt by Ali Pasha in 1811-1812. Clock tower visible from across the city, weapons museum, 800-meter communist-era underground bunker.

The Old Bazaar winds along alleys paved with black and white stone, geometric patterns laid by a single master mason. Built in the 17th century, rebuilt after a fire 200 years later. Olive wood artisans, copper objects, rugs.
Skenduli House, an 18th-century Ottoman mansion, preserves its original carved woodwork. Guided tour by the family who owns it: winter and summer rooms, private hammam, monumental fireplaces.

Zekate House rises on a hill overlooking the city. The house was built in 1812, and its 12 fireplaces testify to the owner's wealth. Corner towers, reception rooms, panoramic view over the stone roofs.
The Bazaar Mosque, sole survivor of the fifteen mosques destroyed under the communist regime. 18th-century Ottoman architecture, slender minaret. Still in use, free entry outside prayer times.

activities.text: Hike to Ali Pasha's Bridge, an old Ottoman aqueduct leading to the castle. Shepherd's trail (45 minutes), view over the Drino valley. Flocks still cross the bridge around 5pm.

visits.text: Lekurësi Castle, an Ottoman fortress on the strategic hill, offers panoramic views over Sarandë, the Ksamil islands and Corfu (Greece) in the distance. Restaurant on site, ideal at sunset.

activities.text: Stroll along Sarandë's palm-lined boulevard. Cafés, fish restaurants on pontoons above the water, entertainment down to the port. Views over the Ionian bay and Corfu 10 km away.
Settle in and relax after the drive. Swimming possible from Sarandë's urban beaches. Seafood dinner on the waterfront.

visits.text: Butrint, a UNESCO archaeological site, preserves successive layers of Greek, Roman and Byzantine civilizations. A 4th-century BC Greek theater remodeled by the Romans, an early Christian baptistery with mosaics, a Byzantine basilica. Forests and lagoons surround the ruins.

The beaches of Ksamil offer stretches of white sand and turquoise waters facing the four islets. Compared to the Maldives of Europe, they attract crowds in July–August. Seafood restaurants, paddleboat rentals for trips to the islands.

activities.text: Rent a paddleboat or kayak to reach the Ksamil islets. Exploration of the four islands, snorkeling in the crystal-clear waters, isolated coves. Return via the main beaches.

practical_info.tip: Rental from the main beach, approximately €10/hour

visits.text: Drymades Beach, near Dhërmi, combines white pebbles and golden sand. The rocky arch on the shore separates sections of the beach. Walk along the water, swim in the turquoise sea and stop at a beach restaurant.

The village of Dhërmi clings to the mountainside at an altitude of 200 meters. Traditional stone houses, Greek Orthodox churches, cobbled alleys. The population speaks the Himariote dialect of Greek and Tosk Albanian.

Drymades Beach mixes white pebbles in the north and golden sand in the south over 1 km. Turquoise waters, natural rock arch on the shore. Beach clubs, restaurants, relaxed atmosphere. Green Coast Resort hosts Albania's only Blue Flag beach.

activities.text: Take a morning walk through the cobbled lanes of Dhërmi's old village. Look at the stone houses and Orthodox churches before heading to Drymades Beach for a swim.

practical_info.tip: Bring swimsuit, water very cold but invigorating

activities.text: Late afternoon relaxation on Drymades beach. Sunbed, swimming, sunset from a beach bar. Chill vibes of the Albanian Riviera.

visits.text: Gjipe Canyon cuts through the mountain to the sea between Vuno and Dhërmi. A marked trail (1–2 hours) offers dizzying views of red rock walls and green vegetation. It leads to the isolated beach of Gjipe, accessible only on foot or by boat.

Gjipe Beach, at the canyon's end, stretches between vertical cliffs, with pebbles and sand. Clear waters, snorkeling, sunbeds for rent. Modest bar-restaurant. One of the most spectacular beaches on the Albanian Riviera.

The old village of Himarë rises up the slopes of Mount Çika at an altitude of 200 meters; allow for a round trip from Dhërmi for this excursion. Cobbled lanes, stone houses and Orthodox churches. The ruins of the Venetian castle overlook the bay. The population is traditionally Himariote Greek.
Potami Beach in Himarë offers fine pebbles, crystal-clear water and a rustic bar-restaurant. Less busy than neighboring beaches. Allow for a round trip from Dhërmi for this excursion.

activities.text: Morning: hike into Gjipe Canyon and swim on the beach at the canyon's end. Afternoon: excursion to Himarë (30 min by car), climb to the Venetian castle for the panorama over the Riviera, return to Dhërmi for sunset.

practical_info.tip: Full day but varied: canyon in the morning, castle in the afternoon

visits.text: Llogara National Park covers 1,020 hectares of black pine and oak forests in the Ceraunian Mountains. Llogara Pass, at 1,027 meters, marks the transition between the Riviera and the bay of Vlorë. It is approximately 39 km from Vlorë, a 50-minute drive. A viewpoint looks down onto the turquoise beaches.
Kaninë Castle has overlooked Vlorë since the 3rd century BC. Founded by the Illyrians, reinforced under Byzantium then the Ottomans. The walls offer panoramic views over the bay and the Adriatic.
The Muradie Mosque (Lead Mosque), designed by architect Mimar Sinan in 1537, is one of the Ottoman jewels of Albania. Octagonal dome, 18-meter minaret, bricks laid in alternating colors.
The Independence Museum occupies the yellow house where Ismail Qemali proclaimed Albanian independence on November 28, 1912. Busts of early prime ministers, period furniture, historical flags.

activities.text: Stop at Llogara Pass, approximately 39 km from Vlorë, a 50-minute drive, for the panoramic view of the Albanian Riviera. Forest trails in the national park (30-60 min). Walk along Vlorë's Lungomare at the end of the day, with views of the Karaburun peninsula.

visits.text: Return to Skanderbeg Square for anything you missed on the first day. The Palace of Culture, the opera house and the clock tower frame the square.

The Pyramid of Tirana, built in 1988 as a museum glorifying Enver Hoxha, was renovated in 2023. Its outer steps can be climbed on foot to the top. The interior now houses a center for young people and technology.

Saint Paul Catholic Cathedral, consecrated in 2002, is recognizable by its modern architecture and stained glass. One window depicts Mother Teresa, born in Skopje to Albanian parents. The building marks the return of worship after 1991.

The Blloku district was reserved for the communist nomenklatura and off-limits to the public until 1991. Enver Hoxha's villa still stands there. The area now has a concentration of Tirana's bars, shops and restaurants.

activities.text: Final stroll along the Boulevard of National Martyrs to the artificial lake in the Grand Park. Souvenir shopping in the center. Farewell dinner at a traditional Tirana restaurant.

seo.h1_title: Albania Road Trip: Sea, Mountains & Complete Itinerary
seo.intro_paragraph: Explore Tirana, lose yourself in Krujë's bazaar, navigate Koman's fjords, trek from Valbona to Theth and unwind on the Albanian Riviera's beaches. In Albania, mountains plunge into a sea still untouched by mass tourism.
seo.seo_hook: Wild fjords, stone villages, UNESCO sites and turquoise bays. Albania is the raw soul of the Balkans, where history whispers through pristine landscapes.
featured_list: Koman: wild fjords of the Albanian Alps
Berat: city of a thousand Ottoman windows
Butrint: Greek ruins by the lagoon
Ksamil: turquoise beaches facing the islets
